title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Top Issues (Playbook)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference focused on: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues with fixes. It is intended for writers, SDK owners, developer advocates, support engineers, and on-call engineers who contribute or maintain public and internal Developer Experience docs.

Purpose and Scope:
- Purpose: Make our SDK docs, quickstarts, and API examples consistent, discoverable, and reliable so customers can integrate Redwood quickly and reduce support friction.
- Scope: All docs under confluence/eng-developer-experience that target end-users or integrators, including: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Templates, Docs site operating procedures, and canonical Top Issues lists.

Ownership and Roles:
- Document owner: the primary author listed in each page's metadata.
- Module owner: the SDK or product engineer responsible for the code examples.
- Reviewer(s): at least one technical reviewer (engineer) and one DevEx reviewer.
- Publishing owner: DevEx Docs team (eng-developer-experience) handles final site publishing and redirects.

Standards for Content Structure (required):
1) Title and short description (one sentence).
2) Audience and prerequisites.
3) Quickstart (2-5 minute path) with copy-paste commands.
4) Examples (incremental): basic -> intermediate -> production.
5) Troubleshooting / Top issues and canonical fixes.
6) API reference links and related pages.
7) Ownership and last updated date (metadata).

Confluence formatting conventions:
- Use H2 for top sections, H3 for subsections.
- Use bullet lists for short steps and numbered lists for sequences.
- Include a small code block for each CLI/SDK snippet; keep examples < 30 lines when possible.
- Add a short table for configuration values or SLOs.

Templates (copy & use) - front matter and skeleton:
- Required front matter: title, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated, reviewers, labels, related_pages, confidentiality.
- Quickstart template (skeleton):
  1) Short intro (1-2 sentences).
  2) Prereqs (API key, CLI/SDK version).
  3) Quickstart steps (numbered).
  4) Expected output (code block or JSON).
  5) Next steps and links.

Example Quickstart (Node + REST):
1) Prereqs: Node 18+, npm, Redwood API key with demo access.
2) Install: npm install @redwood-inference/sdk
3) Run:
   ```js
   import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk';
   const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
   const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'gptx-2.7b', prompt: 'Translate to French: Hello' });
   console.log(resp.text);
   ```
4) Expected: a short French translation returned in resp.text.

API Examples: best practices:
- Provide at least two language examples (Python and JavaScript).
- Prefer the official SDK for examples; include a curl/REST example for quick debugging.
- Annotate examples with where to change values (API key, model id, prompt).
- Include a minimal example for streaming responses and for embeddings (embedding vectors usage).

Docs Site Operating Procedures (publish & rollback):
1) Draft: author writes doc in Confluence local page with required front matter.
2) Review: request review from listed reviewers via Slack #devex-docs; reviewers have 3 business days to respond.
3) QA: run examples locally; verify samples succeed with latest SDK (CI test below).
4) Publish: DevEx owner merges to docs site and updates the navigation index.
5) Post-publish smoke test: run the smoke examples with a fresh environment and record results in the page's comments.
6) Rollback: if a regression is reported, set status to in_review, add a pinned banner at page top, and revert the site commit within 2 hours for severe breakages.

CI / Verification for examples:
- Every docs PR that changes code snippets must include a `docs-e2e` job that runs the official SDK examples against a sandbox API key.
- Failure thresholds: tests must pass on main; flaky failures require an incident review.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (common patterns):
- Issue: Authentication errors (401)
  - Cause: missing/expired API key or wrong env var.
  - Fix: Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY is set and has correct scopes; show `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY` and example curl.
- Issue: Streaming responses hang or cut off
  - Cause: client not handling chunked transfer or socket timeouts.
  - Fix: provide streaming client sample (Node fetch with keepalive) and recommend SDK streaming helper.
- Issue: Unexpected tokenization / token budget exceeded
  - Cause: model length + prompt too long; default max_tokens set too low/unsupported.
  - Fix: Show how to compute token estimates, set max_tokens and truncation policy.
- Issue: Embedding vectors differ between SDK versions
  - Cause: quantization/model-version changes.
  - Fix: Pin model version in example and document migration steps and reindexing guidance.

Canonical Fix Template (for each top issue page):
- Symptom: short description of user-visible symptom.
- Diagnostic commands: 2-4 commands that reveal the underlying cause.
- Root cause: one-paragraph technical reason.
- Fix steps: numbered, reproducible steps.
- Acceptance: how the user confirms the fix (expected outputs).

Ownership and Review Checklist (required before publishing):
- [ ] Title and short description present.
- [ ] Quickstart can be completed in < 10 minutes.
- [ ] Code samples run successfully against `docs-e2e` sandbox.
- [ ] Security review performed if samples handle secrets or PII.
- [ ] Reviewer sign-off in page metadata.
- [ ] Labels and related_pages set for discoverability.

Metrics and Observability for Docs Health:
- Time-to-first-success: median time from new user sign-up to successful quickstart completion (tracked in onboarding funnel).
- Support deflection rate: number of support tickets referencing a doc after doc update (goal: reduce).
- Docs CI pass rate for code snippets.

Retention and Deprecation Policy:
- Deprecate examples tied to SDK versions older than 12 months; mark pages with a deprecation banner and provide migration guide.
- Archive deprecated quickstarts in `/archive` section with an alternative link.

Appendix: Example Troubleshooting Table:
| Symptom | Likely cause | Quick check | Canonical fix page |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 401 Unauthorized | Missing/invalid API key | curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/v1 | confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/authentication-troubleshooting |
| Streaming stops mid-response | Client timeout | run streaming client locally | confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/streaming-canonical-fixes |

Frequently referenced pages and templates:
- Developer Experience Docs Playbook (root): confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/developer-experience-docs-playbook-2026.json
- SDK quickstart template: confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/developer-experience-sdk-quickstarts-and-api-examples-2026.json

Contact and escalation:
- Primary: DevEx Docs team (devex-docs@redwood.com).
- Urgent publishing/rollback: #devex-docs on Slack (pager duty rotation: see owner metadata).

Change log (brief):
- 2026-01-15: Initial draft (Aisha Patel).
- 2026-02-10: Added CI verification steps and canonical fixes list (Marco Li).
